messages:
Mira Patel: Hey team — ACME wants their trial environment to stream POC telemetry (audit logs + request traces) to their Splunk SIEM for 30 days. They also asked which evidence we can provide for the security questionnaire.
Zach Kim: Quick q — do they need full request/response bodies or just headers/metadata? Splunk ingest cost could balloon if bodies included.
Mira Patel: They said 'full' initially but will accept metadata if we can show deterministic sampling and explain retention. Pricing ask: they want an estimate of incremental cost for 30 days of full telemetry versus metadata-only.
Priya Rao: For Hosted API keys we can provide request-level logs (no raw customer prompt text stored by default). For Dedicated/Private we can enable configurable export pipelines. Need to confirm ACME's exact requirement on PII in payloads.
Sam Torres: I'll scope options: 1) Hosted -> push logs to our S3 export (we can share manifests and signed URL), ACME pulls into Splunk; 2) Hosted -> we push to Splunk HEC (requires HEC token and endpoint); 3) Dedicated/Private -> we can ship raw logs to their VPC or partner collector.
Mira Patel: They prefer push to their Splunk HEC to avoid extra pull steps. They can provide an HEC endpoint and token. Any infra blockers?
infra-bot: Ticket INF-4721 created: splunk-hec-poc -> assignee: @Sam Torres. ETA: initial config by EOD + checklist for security evidence.
Sam Torres: OK, need ACME's HEC URL, team-maintained token, and the customer CIDR for whitelisting. Also need confirmation on whether they want TLS mutual auth.
Zach Kim: On evidence: we can provide export of audit logs (S3), CloudTrail-style delivery for infra actions, access control list screenshots, and a signed statement of retained logs for the POC window. We should prepare a short manifest they can attach to the questionnaire.
Priya Rao: Also add config snippets and the retention policy we apply. For Dedicated/Private we can hand over KMS-wrapped log objects if they require customer-managed keys.
Mira Patel: ACME asked about timeframe — how long to get HEC ingest active?
Sam Torres: If they provide HEC endpoint + token + allowlist quickly, we can enable test streaming within 24 hours (non-business-hours may add slight delay). Full 30-day retention/reporting ready same day after enabling.
Mira Patel: Pricing note — rough delta: metadata-only ≈ negligible, full-body streaming ~ +$0.05–0.12 per 1k lines depending on storage/egress — will confirm with finance.
Zach Kim: For the questionnaire items (they asked for 'evidence of log integrity'), suggest we provide: md5 checksums per daily archive, S3 object versioning enabled, and a short note on access control and rotation of the export credentials.
Priya Rao: Ops ask: who owns the signed manifest? Sales or Security? I can help draft but need signoff for accuracy.
Mira Patel: I'll own the manifest but please tag Security for review. @Zach can you draft the technical appendix?
Zach Kim: Yep will draft tech appendix and example S3 manifest. Will include example curl to validate HEC receipt: ```curl -X POST "https://splunk.acme.example/services/collector/event" -H "Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>" -d '{"event":"test","severity":"info"}'```
Sam Torres: One more infra caveat: if they want raw prompt bodies, we need an MCC (data processing addendum) signed. Legal already flagged that for Dedicated/Private customers.
Mira Patel: Good call. I'll loop in Legal if they insist on raw bodies.
infra-bot: Reminder — checklist created at https://internal.redwood/tasks/INF-4721/checklist (for internal use).
Mira Patel: Thanks — I'll update ACME with options and timeline. Will post back here after they send HEC details. :thumbsup:
